summary: Rules-only assessment: ownership and role guards held in emulator tests, but the current app group schema is rejected while malformed group plans are accepted; full group setup is readable by any signed-in holder of its code. This is not an overall application security score.

findings.issue: validSetup rejects current Setup.toJson fields and treats skipped books as weekday IDs, preventing current group creation.
findings.recommendation: Align the shared schema and use actual serialized app fixtures for create and update tests.

findings.issue: Any signed-in user knowing a group code can read the entire group setup, including pending and rejected members, although the UI restricts plan access to approved members.
findings.recommendation: Separate join preview metadata from approved-member-only plan documents.

findings.issue: Group rules accept nonexistent book pointers and impossible calendar dates. A rule-accepted book pointer breaks client planning.
findings.recommendation: Validate actual book/chapter limits and dates server-side and before client rendering.

findings.issue: Document fields and collection entries have bounds, but arbitrary private map values lack per-entry validation and client decoding can fail. No per-user document-count/rate control is shown.
findings.recommendation: Validate an entire candidate snapshot before applying it; consider schema migration, monitored App Check rollout and quota/abuse controls.
